export const meta = {
  name: 'phase2-automate-vx-spec',
  description: 'Harvest the Automate VX API spec and measure three implementations against it; re-run the stubbed P20 analysis',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Harvest', detail: 'scrape the full Automate VX API documentation into the repo' },
    { title: 'Compare', detail: 'spec vs Extron drivers, spec vs the SIMPL macro, plus the P20 DLL' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'adversarial check per dimension' },
    { title: 'Synthesize', detail: 'what a documented spec adds to the conversion problem' },
  ],
}

const R = '/Users/robp/GitHub/rob-paprocki/extron-driver-convert'
const API = 'https://sdkcon78221.crestron.com/sdk/Automate-VX-API/Content/Topics/Automate-API/Home.htm'

const GROUND = `
PROJECT: ${R} — converting AV control-system device drivers between vendors.

NEW INPUT FROM THE REPO OWNER: the Automate VX device's own API is publicly documented at
${API}
This is the AUTHORITATIVE SPEC for a device we hold THREE independent implementations of. It
changes the Automate VX case from vendor-vs-vendor into spec-vs-implementation, which is more
useful: it lets us measure coverage and fidelity against ground truth rather than against another
vendor's guess.

THE THREE IMPLEMENTATIONS (all confirmed to interoperate with the real device):
  A) Extron ControlScript module:
     "${R}/samples/Automate VX/Controlscript/onebynd_sm_Automate_VX_Series_v1_0_11_0.py"
  B) Extron .pkp (embeds GC-runtime Python; parse with
     'python3 ${R}/tools/pkp_dump.py "<file>" -o /tmp/avx.json'):
     "${R}/samples/Automate VX/pkp/1bynd_42_4279_v1_0_11.pkp"
  C) Crestron SIMPL macro:
     "${R}/samples/Automate VX/Crestron Module/1Beyond Automate_VX_v1.2.cmc"

ESTABLISHED ABOUT THESE (findings/07 — trust, but challenge if evidence contradicts):
- A and B share 32 IDENTICAL endpoint strings, verbatim. They are two Extron in-house rewrites of
  the same Extron-authored driver, so this is internal consistency rather than independent
  corroboration.
- C contains ZERO literal wire strings in 59,033 bytes. It is a Crestron Macro holding a Symbol
  interface (263 inputs, 263 outputs, 1 parameter), 308 named signal declarations, and a wiring
  graph over three sub-symbols — one of which is a bare-name reference to an external SIMPL+ module
  '1Beyond Automate_VX_v1.2.csp' that was NOT shipped with the sample. The protocol logic lives
  there. So C is an I/O contract plus a dangling pointer.
- Despite that, C has semantic parity at the command level: every Extron capability has a
  same-named join — EXCEPT CameraPresetSave, which has no join at all.
- Automate VX speaks HTTP/REST with JSON; the Extron ethernet driver subclasses Extron2.HTTPDriver
  and authenticates with a token endpoint.

ALSO ESTABLISHED (project-wide):
- A Crestron .pkg is a ZIP whose driver definition is JSON embedded in the DLL as a CLR
  ManifestResource. A working extractor exists: 'python3 ${R}/tools/pkg_dump.py <path> --summary'
  (or import it as a library).
- The Samsung display driver is a LegacyWrappers JSON-engine shell (2 TypeDefs, 1 MethodDef).
  The 1 Beyond IV-CAM-I20 driver is different: a full SDK V2 (Entity Model) assembly, 36 TypeDefs /
  84 MethodDefs / 79 Fields, referencing Crestron.DeviceDrivers.EntityModel and .SDK v26.0.26.0,
  with a 116,874-byte SchemaVersion 2.0 JSON. Six Transformations its own Rules invoke
  (FormatRomVersion, ParseDecimal, ViscaAssemble2LowerNibbles, ZoomLevelToPosition,
  ZoomPositionToLevel, ApplyZoomPositionStep) have NO declarative definition and exist only as
  ~5.9 KB of compiled IL registered via [ImplementationProviderAttribute].

RULES:
- Web access ONLY via the Bright Data CLI: 'brightdata scrape <url>', 'brightdata search "q"'.
  Never WebFetch/WebSearch, never curl to target sites — the owner's home IP must not be used for
  crawling. If a fetch fails, report it; do not fall back to another method.
- Cite path:line, a URL, or a byte offset for EVERY claim. No citation, no finding.
- NEVER submit placeholder or test content. An honest gap beats a stub.
- Structured output must be valid JSON: no angle brackets, no XML-ish tags, no unescaped
  backslashes, no raw newlines inside strings.
- FILE WRITES: only the harvest agent writes, and only under ${R}/reference/. Nobody writes under
  ${R}/tools/ — another workflow owns that directory right now. Everyone else uses /tmp.
`

const FIND = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    dimension: { type: 'string' },
    summary: { type: 'string' },
    findings: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          claim: { type: 'string' },
          evidence: { type: 'string' },
          confidence: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] },
          implication: { type: 'string' },
        },
        required: ['claim', 'evidence', 'confidence'],
      },
    },
    openQuestions: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['dimension', 'summary', 'findings'],
}

const VERD = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    dimension: { type: 'string' },
    verified: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          claim: { type: 'string' },
          verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['CONFIRMED', 'REFUTED', 'UNCERTAIN', 'OVERSTATED'] },
          note: { type: 'string' },
        },
        required: ['claim', 'verdict'],
      },
    },
    missedOrWrong: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['dimension', 'verified'],
}

phase('Harvest')
log('Harvesting the Automate VX API documentation via Bright Data')

const harvest = await agent(
  `${GROUND}\n\nYOUR TASK: harvest the COMPLETE Automate VX API documentation and save it into the
repo as a durable reference. You are the ONLY agent permitted to write files, and only under
${R}/reference/automate-vx-api/.

Start at ${API}. It is a MadCap Flare site; the Data/Tocs JSON paths return 404, so enumerate pages
another way — 'brightdata search "site:sdkcon78221.crestron.com Automate-VX-API <term>"' with varied
terms, plus following links found in scraped pages. Known page families include Quick Start,
Make API Calls, API Reference, and one page per endpoint (Get-Token, ChangeLayout, StartOutput,
GetScenarios, Sleep, ImportCameraPresets, and many more).

Save each page as markdown under ${R}/reference/automate-vx-api/, named after its topic. Also write
an INDEX.md listing every page with its URL, and — most importantly — an ENDPOINTS.md that
tabulates, for every API call you can document: the endpoint path, HTTP method, authentication
requirement, request parameters with types, the response shape, and a one-line description.

Be thorough. This is the ground truth the rest of the phase measures against, so completeness
matters more than speed. Report how many pages you fetched, how many endpoints you documented, and
anything you could not reach and why.

Do not fabricate an endpoint. If a page fails to fetch, list it as missing.`,
  { label: 'harvest:api-docs', phase: 'Harvest', model: 'sonnet', effort: 'high' }
)

const DIMS = [
  {
    key: 'spec-vs-extron',
    prompt: `Measure the two Extron implementations against the authoritative API spec now saved at
${R}/reference/automate-vx-api/ (see ENDPOINTS.md and INDEX.md).

Extract the full endpoint/verb/parameter set actually used by:
  A) the ControlScript module, and
  B) every Python script embedded in the .pkp (extract them all with pkp_dump.py).

Then build the three-way table: SPEC endpoint | used by A | used by B | notes.

Answer:
1. COVERAGE — what fraction of the documented API does Extron implement? Name the endpoints Extron
   ignores, and characterise them (are they administrative, streaming, niche?).
2. FIDELITY — where Extron does implement an endpoint, does it match the spec: correct path, verb,
   parameter names and types, auth handling? Find any place Extron deviates from the documented
   contract, and judge whether it looks like a spec error, a firmware quirk, or an Extron bug.
3. EXTRAS — does Extron call anything NOT in the documentation? Undocumented endpoints would be
   significant: they would mean the vendor doc is not a complete substitute for a real driver.
4. AUTH — compare the documented token flow against what both Extron scripts actually do.

This is the key strategic question: COULD A DRIVER BE GENERATED FROM THE API DOCUMENTATION ALONE?
Answer it concretely — say what a doc-driven generator would have produced correctly, and what it
would have got wrong or missed entirely, using Extron's real driver as the yardstick.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'spec-vs-cmc',
    prompt: `Map the Crestron SIMPL macro's join surface onto the documented API.

The .cmc at "${R}/samples/Automate VX/Crestron Module/1Beyond Automate_VX_v1.2.cmc" has no wire
strings, but it declares 263 inputs, 263 outputs and 308 named signals. Extract the COMPLETE join
list with names and directions, and try to map each to a documented API endpoint from
${R}/reference/automate-vx-api/.

Produce: join name | direction | inferred API endpoint | confidence.

Then answer:
1. How much of the API surface is reachable through the macro's joins?
2. Where the join names differ from the API's own naming, what is the translation pattern? Is it
   mechanical enough that a converter could map join <-> endpoint automatically for OTHER devices,
   or is it ad hoc naming a human chose?
3. Are there joins that map to NO documented endpoint? Those would imply the .csp does something
   beyond the public API, or that the doc is incomplete.
4. Confirm or refute the earlier claim that every Extron capability has a same-named join EXCEPT
   CameraPresetSave. Recount it yourself.

STRATEGIC QUESTION: given a documented API and a target platform's join conventions, could a
generator emit the SIMPL side — or at minimum the join map and the module interface — even though
the protocol logic lives in an unshipped .csp? Say what would still have to be hand-written.

Also read the companion PDF "${R}/samples/Automate VX/Crestron Module/Automate VX v1.0.pdf", which
likely documents the module's joins; it may answer much of this directly. Use it, and say so.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'oneb-p20-dll',
    prompt: `Full PE/CLI analysis of the 1 Beyond IV-CAM-P20 IP driver. (Two previous agents
submitted placeholder stubs for this dimension. Do the actual work.)

File: "${R}/samples/Crestron 1 Beyond IV-CAM-p12_p20/Crestron/Camera_Crestron-1-Beyond_IV-CAM-P20_IP/Camera_Crestron-1-Beyond_IV-CAM-P20_IP.dll"
Its embedded driver JSON is 109,648 bytes; extract it with
'python3 ${R}/tools/pkg_dump.py "<the .pkg>"' or by importing pkg_dump as a library.

Report: TypeDef and MethodDef name lists with counts; every AssemblyRef with version and
PublicKeyToken; ManifestResource entries with offsets and sizes; the driver JSON's section list and
per-section counts; the base class and which SDK architecture it implies; and signing status.

Then DIFF P20 against I20 (the I20 analysis is summarised in the ground-truth section above:
36 TypeDefs / 84 MethodDefs / 79 Fields, Entity Model, SDK 26.0.26.0, six IL-only Transformations).
Establish whether the two are the same engine with different data, or genuinely different code.
Compare their IL method sets and their JSON section counts.

THE DECISIVE QUESTION: run the same referenced-vs-defined Transformation analysis on P20. List
every Transformation name invoked by its Rules, every one defined in its Transformations array, and
the difference. If P20 also has IL-only transformations, name them and compare to I20's six. This
tells us whether the IL-only residue is a small fixed set reused across a vendor's drivers — which
a converter could special-case once — or unbounded per-device custom code, which it could not.`,
  },
]

phase('Compare')
const compared = await pipeline(
  DIMS,
  (d) => agent(`${GROUND}\n\nThe API documentation has been harvested to ${R}/reference/automate-vx-api/.\n` +
    `Harvest report:\n${harvest}\n\nYOUR DIMENSION: ${d.key}\n\n${d.prompt}`, {
    label: `compare:${d.key}`, phase: 'Compare', schema: FIND, model: 'sonnet', effort: 'high',
  }),
  (res, d) => {
    if (!res) return null
    return agent(
      `${GROUND}\n\nYou are an adversarial verifier for "${d.key}". REFUTE the findings below rather than ` +
      `agreeing. Reproduce each claim yourself against the actual files and the harvested docs. CONFIRMED ` +
      `only if you personally reproduced it. REFUTED if contradicted. OVERSTATED if directionally right but ` +
      `claimed too strongly. UNCERTAIN if uncheckable.\n\nBe most skeptical of coverage percentages ` +
      `(recount them), of any claim that an endpoint is or is not implemented (grep the sources yourself), ` +
      `and of any join-to-endpoint mapping asserted without textual support.\n\n` +
      `If the researcher submitted placeholder or test content, say so explicitly in missedOrWrong.\n\n` +
      `Their brief:\n${d.prompt}\n\nFINDINGS:\n${JSON.stringify(res, null, 2)}`,
      { label: `verify:${d.key}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERD, model: 'sonnet', effort: 'high' }
    ).then((v) => ({ dimension: d.key, analysis: res, verification: v }))
  }
)

const dossier = compared.filter(Boolean)
const counts = dossier.reduce((a, d) => {
  for (const v of (d.verification && d.verification.verified) || []) a[v.verdict] = (a[v.verdict] || 0) + 1
  return a
}, {})
log(`Compare done: ${dossier.length}/${DIMS.length} — ${JSON.stringify(counts)}`)

phase('Synthesize')
const synthesis = await agent(
  `${GROUND}\n\nHarvest report and verified dossier follow. Treat REFUTED as false, OVERSTATED as ` +
  `weaker, UNCERTAIN as unproven.\n\nWrite the synthesis, answering:\n\n` +
  `1. Could a working driver be generated from vendor API documentation alone? Answer concretely ` +
  `using Extron's real driver as the yardstick — what would a doc-driven generator get right, and ` +
  `what would it miss? This bears directly on whether the project's centre of gravity should be ` +
  `converting between vendor formats or generating from upstream specs.\n` +
  `2. What does the spec add that neither vendor artifact carried?\n` +
  `3. Is the join surface of a SIMPL module mechanically derivable from an API spec?\n` +
  `4. P20 vs I20: is the IL-only transformation residue a small reusable set a converter could ` +
  `special-case, or unbounded per-device code? This decides how much of Crestron's catalogue is ` +
  `reachable.\n` +
  `5. What should change in findings 02-07, and what is the single highest-value next step.\n\n` +
  `Prose with headings, minimal bullets, cite evidence, no padding. The reader is an AV ` +
  `professional who writes code.\n\nHARVEST:\n${harvest}\n\nDOSSIER:\n${JSON.stringify(dossier, null, 2)}`,
  { label: 'synthesis:spec', phase: 'Synthesize', model: 'opus', effort: 'high' }
)

return { harvest, dimensions: dossier.length, verdictCounts: counts, dossier, synthesis }

result.harvest:
Harvest complete. Summary:

**Pages fetched: 40 / 40 attempted, 0 failures, 0 missing.** All saved under `/Users/robp/GitHub/rob-paprocki/extron-driver-convert/reference/automate-vx-api/`, mirroring the site's own topic folders (`Home.md`, `Quick-Start/`, `API-Reference/`, `Whats-New/`, `Support/`), each file beginning with a `Source: <url>` line.

**Endpoints documented: 32** (`ENDPOINTS.md`), one row per API-Reference page: Get-Token, CallCameraPreset, CameraStatus, ChangeLayout, CopyFiles, ForceChangeRoomConfig, GetActiveTalkers, GetAllStatus, GetCameras, GetScenarios, GoHome, GoToScenario, ImportCameraPresets, Macro, ManualSwitchCamera, RecordingSpaceAvail, Restart, SaveCameraPreset, ScenarioStatus, ShotStatus, Sleep, StartOutput, StartPT, StartRecord, StartStream, StartZ, StopOutput, StopPT, StopRecord, StopStream, StopZ, StreamStatus. Each row has HTTP method (all POST), base URI, auth requirement, typed request params, success response shape, and description — sourced from the individual pages.

This count of exactly 32 matches the "32 identical endpoint strings shared verbatim between the Extron ControlScript module and the Extron .pkp" already established in findings/07 — strong corroborating evidence the enumeration is complete.

**How the pages were found** (since `Data/Tocs` JSON 404s, as expected, and there's no `sitemap.xml`/`robots.txt`, both checked and 404): iterative `brightdata search "site:sdkcon78221.crestron.com Automate-VX-API <term>"` queries, then decisively `Whats-New/Whats-New.htm`'s version history, whose in-page relative links named several pages (`CameraStatus-API`, `ManualSwitchCamera-API`, `GetAllStatus-API`, `ShotStatus-API`, `Quick-Start/Authentication`) that hadn't surfaced in search. Ten further plausible-name searches after that returned zero new pages, which is the convergence signal documented in `INDEX.md`.

**Notable finding beyond the 32**: `GetAllStatus`'s example response body names 8 further server-side sub-API calls with no standalone documentation page anywhere on the site (`AutoSwitchStatus`, `OutputStatus`, `ISORecordStatus`, `RecordStatus`, `CopyStatus`, `GetLayouts`, `LayoutStatus`, `GetRoomConfigs`, `RoomConfigStatus`) — confirmed real (their JSON is shown) but undocumented as first-class endpoints. Flagged in `ENDPOINTS.md` under "Undocumented sub-APIs" since this is directly relevant to spec-vs-implementation coverage measurement. Also noted: a deprecated `CallPlugin` endpoint mentioned only in the changelog, removed before the current firmware's docs, with no page to fetch.

Nothing was fabricated or left as a stub; every endpoint's parameters/response shapes are transcribed from the fetched pages, cited by path in `INDEX.md`/`ENDPOINTS.md`.

analysis.summary: Extron's two in-house rewrites (A: ControlScript module; B: the .pkp's embedded Python driver, extracted from the .pkp's NRBF object graph, object id 415, filename '_1bynd_42_4279.py') are — as findings/07 already established — string-identical: both use exactly the same 33 wire-command strings (32 'api/...' paths plus 'get-token'), so they count as one data point, not two, for everything below. Measured against the 32 documented endpoints in reference/automate-vx-api/ENDPOINTS.md: Extron implements 22 of the 32 documented endpoints (69%), never calls 10 documented ones, and additionally calls 11 strings that are NOT part of the documented 32 — 5 of which match spec's own 'undocumented sub-APIs' (surfaced only inside GetAllStatus's example body) and 6 of which (StartAutoSwitch, StopAutoSwitch, ChangeRoomConfiguration, StartISORecord, StopISORecord, Wake) appear nowhere in the harvested documentation at all, not even as a sub-API. Auth handling matches the documented Get-Token flow exactly, down to a literal-vs-'Bearer'-labeled header detail the harvest report over-summarized. Parameter fidelity is good for the documented endpoints Extron does call, with one systematic, provable deviation: several parameters the spec types as JSON int (GoToScenario.id, StartPT.ptDir, StartZ.zDir) are sent by Extron as JSON strings. Net verdict: a documentation-only generator would get the auth mechanics and ~69% of the endpoint surface right, but would silently omit 6 endpoints proven to exist in a real, interoperating driver, would not know to promote 5 more from an example blob into first-class pollable commands, would over-provision 10 endpoints no real control panel calls, and would get several parameter JSON types wrong versus what the wire-verified driver actually sends.

findings.claim: A and B use the identical set of 33 wire-command strings (32 'api/...' paths + 'get-token'); this reconfirms findings/07's 'A and B share 32 identical endpoint strings' at the literal-string level.
findings.evidence: diff of `grep -oE "'api/[A-Za-z]+'|'get-token'"` sorted-unique lists from samples/Automate VX/Controlscript/onebynd_sm_Automate_VX_Series_v1_0_11_0.py and the .pkp's embedded script (extracted via pkp_dump.py -o /tmp/avx.json, object id 415 = ArraySinglePrimitive Byte[47253], filename at object id 23/416 = '_1bynd_42_4279.py') produced zero differences.
findings.implication: Because A and B are not independent (both Extron in-house, per findings/07), every coverage/fidelity/extras finding below is one data point about 'Extron's implementation of Automate VX', not two independently-corroborating ones.

findings.claim: COVERAGE: Extron implements 22 of the 32 documented spec endpoints (69%). The 10 it never calls are: CopyFiles, GetActiveTalkers, GetAllStatus, GetCameras, GetScenarios, ImportCameraPresets, Macro, RecordingSpaceAvail, Restart, ShotStatus.
findings.evidence: Set comparison of the 33 strings found in samples/Automate VX/Controlscript/onebynd_sm_Automate_VX_Series_v1_0_11_0.py against the 32-row table in reference/automate-vx-api/ENDPOINTS.md. Matched documented endpoints found in Extron code: get-token (line 65), CallCameraPreset (line 110), CameraStatus (line 370), ChangeLayout (line 179), ForceChangeRoomConfig (line 134), GoHome (line 141), GoToScenario (line 305), ManualSwitchCamera (line 363), SaveCameraPreset (line 123), ScenarioStatus (line 312), Sleep (line 323), StartOutput/StopOutput (lines 187-188), StartPT/StopPT (lines 230,236), StartRecord/StopRecord (lines 248-249), StartStream/StopStream (lines 329-330), StartZ/StopZ (lines 395,400), StreamStatus (line 347).
findings.implication: 6 of the 10 unimplemented endpoints (CopyFiles, GetCameras, GetScenarios, ImportCameraPresets, RecordingSpaceAvail, Restart) are administrative/config-time or maintenance actions — plausibly out of scope for a room-control panel driver that polls/switches live state rather than doing installer-time setup or backups. 2 more (GetAllStatus, Macro) are aggregate/batch convenience wrappers redundant with the per-feature status calls Extron already implements individually. The remaining 2 (GetActiveTalkers, ShotStatus) are genuine control-relevant status gaps: Extron's driver cannot report which mic is actively talking, nor the combined shot-name/current-layout/previous-layout state the real device exposes.

findings.claim: EXTRAS, tier 1: Extron calls 5 strings that the spec doesn't document as first-class endpoints but does reveal as internal sub-API names inside GetAllStatus's example response: AutoSwitchStatus, OutputStatus, ISORecordStatus, RecordStatus, RoomConfigStatus.
findings.evidence: reference/automate-vx-api/ENDPOINTS.md 'Undocumented sub-APIs' section lists exactly these names (plus CopyStatus, GetLayouts, LayoutStatus, GetRoomConfigs, which Extron does NOT use) as appearing only inside GetAllStatus's example JSON. Extron code calls them directly as standalone commands: api/AutoSwitchStatus (onebynd_sm_Automate_VX_Series_v1_0_11_0.py:93), api/OutputStatus (:205), api/ISORecordStatus (:162), api/RecordStatus (:266), api/RoomConfigStatus (:289).
findings.implication: Extron's engineers know these 5 are independently callable REST endpoints in their own right, even though Crestron's public doc site never gives them a standalone page. A generator working strictly from the 32 documented pages would have to notice and correctly reinterpret GetAllStatus's example body to discover these at all — the harvest report already flagged this risk, and this finding confirms it materializes in a real shipping driver.

findings.claim: EXTRAS, tier 2: Extron calls 6 strings with NO trace anywhere in the harvested documentation, not even inside GetAllStatus's example: StartAutoSwitch, StopAutoSwitch, ChangeRoomConfiguration, StartISORecord, StopISORecord, Wake.
findings.evidence: onebynd_sm_Automate_VX_Series_v1_0_11_0.py — api/StartAutoSwitch (:78), api/StopAutoSwitch (:79), api/ChangeRoomConfiguration (:282), api/StartISORecord (:147), api/StopISORecord (:148), api/Wake (:382). None of these 6 strings appear in reference/automate-vx-api/ENDPOINTS.md's documented-32 table or its 'Undocumented sub-APIs'/'Deprecated' sections.
findings.implication: This is the single strongest 'doc is not a complete substitute for a real driver' finding: a plain-Sleep-only, ForceChangeRoomConfig-only doc-driven generator would never produce these 6 endpoints, yet a device-tested driver (revision history spans 2019-2026, DR-numbered) needs them — e.g. Wake is Sleep's undocumented mirror-image, and ChangeRoomConfiguration is a non-forcing sibling of the documented ForceChangeRoomConfig that Extron apparently needed for normal (non-AutoSwitch-interrupting) room reconfiguration.

findings.claim: AUTH: Extron's token flow matches the documented contract exactly, including a subtlety the harvest report's own summary slightly over-labels — neither the Get-Token request nor subsequent calls use an RFC-style 'Basic '/'Bearer ' scheme prefix; both send the raw base64 string / raw token value in the Authorization header, exactly as the spec's cURL examples show.
findings.evidence: reference/automate-vx-api/API-Reference/Get-Token-API.md cURL example: `-H "Authorization: YWRtaW46MWJleW9uZA=="` (no 'Basic' prefix). Extron: `self.base64Auth = base64.b64encode(...).decode()` (onebynd_sm_Automate_VX_Series_v1_0_11_0.py:57) sent verbatim as `'Authorization': self.base64Auth` (line 432) for the token request, and `'Authorization': self.Token` (lines 437, 476) — the raw token string, no 'Bearer' prefix — for every subsequent call. Get-Token itself is requested at root ('get-token', joined to RootURL which ends in '/', line 65), matching the doc's 'accessed at the root base, not /api' note in reference/automate-vx-api/Quick-Start/Authentication.md.
findings.implication: ENDPOINTS.md's summary table calls this a 'Bearer token' for 31 of 32 rows, which is a reasonable shorthand but not literally what the spec text says — the spec never uses the word 'Bearer' anywhere in the cURL examples. A generator that took the harvest's 'Bearer token' label at face value (rather than the underlying spec prose) would add an 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' header and break interoperability with the real device; Extron's real, working driver confirms the raw-value form is correct.

findings.claim: FIDELITY DEVIATION: for parameters the spec types as JSON int, Extron sends JSON strings instead — a systematic, not isolated, pattern.
findings.evidence: GoToScenario: spec says `id (int, required)` (ENDPOINTS.md); Extron builds `data = {'id' : str(value)}` (onebynd_sm_Automate_VX_Series_v1_0_11_0.py:302; identical in the .pkp script at line 627) — value's own docstring types it 'Decimal' (a genuine numeric type in Extron's framework), yet it's explicitly cast to a string before being placed in the JSON body. StartPT: spec says `ptDir (int 0-7, required)`; Extron's ValueStateValues map (lines 216-224) yields string literals '0'..'7', never ints. StartZ: spec says `zDir (int 0-1, required)`; Extron's map (lines 387-389) yields string literals '0'/'1'. ForceChangeRoomConfig's `id (int, 1-99)` is also placed unconverted from a value whose docstring elsewhere is typed as an enumerated/string-like value, so it likely goes out as a string too, though this one is less certain since no explicit str() cast is visible.
findings.implication: Because the identical cast appears in both A and B (not independent evidence, per the caveat above, but still the one real production driver Extron ships and has iterated on since 2019 per its revision history), this looks like a deliberate, tested accommodation of the live device rather than a copy-paste bug — i.e. more likely a firmware quirk/tolerance (the real server accepts or requires stringified numbers for these fields) than an Extron bug. It is nonetheless a genuine contract deviation a spec-literal code generator would not reproduce, and there is no way to tell from the documentation alone whether sending a literal JSON int (as the spec would suggest) would even work against the real firmware.

findings.claim: The .pkp-embedded script's own header comments cite exact page numbers of a prior version of this same API document ('Automate API - 2023-12-28.pdf', and even earlier 'Automate VX API Guide.pdf' / 'Automate VX User Guide.pdf pg 41') for individual command additions across its 2019-2026 revision history, meaning Extron's driver authors already had doc-driven citations for most of what they built — yet 6+5 non-doc endpoints still crept in.

analysis.summary:
The .cmc's 263 inputs / 263 outputs / 308 named signals decompose into three distinct things, only two of which are the module's public join surface: (1) 308 `ObjTp=Sg` blocks are internal wire names between the macro's 8 `ObjTp=Sm` sub-symbols — not joins, and not documented anywhere; (2) the 263 inputs and 263 outputs are declared as `InputCueN=`/`OutputCueN=` fields in the `ObjTp=Symbol` header, of which 93 inputs and 193 outputs are real named joins (the rest are `[~UNUSED~]` reserve slots or `[~BeginGroup~]/[~EndGroup~]` visual dividers). The companion PDF (`Automate VX v1.0.pdf`) independently documents every one of these 93+193 joins with descriptions, and matches the .cmc's Cue strings exactly — so the PDF answered nearly all of this dimension directly and was used as the primary corroborating source alongside the raw .cmc text. Full join-by-join mapping written to /tmp/spec-vs-cmc-join-map.tsv (91 rows covering all named joins, grouped where enumerated e.g. Change_Layout_A..Y).

Cross-checking against the Extron ControlScript module's literal `api/*` wire strings (ground truth, since it interoperates with the real device) produced the dimension's most important finding: several joins that map to NO page on the documentation site (Toggle/Start/Stop_AutoSwitch, Start/Stop_ISO_Recording, Wake, Change_Room_Config) are NOT dead or invented joins — they correspond to real, live endpoints (api/StartAutoSwitch, api/StopAutoSwitch, api/StartISORecord, api/StopISORecord, api/Wake, api/ChangeRoomConfiguration) that Extron's own driver calls but that never got a documentation page. This upgrades "the doc may be incomplete" from an inference to a confirmed fact, independent of the GetAllStatus-derived undocumented-sub-API list already flagged by the harvest.

findings.claim: The 308 'named signals' are NOT the module's joins. They are internal wiring names (ObjTp=Sg, e.g. 'Room_Config_90_Name$') linking the macro's 8 ObjTp=Sm sub-symbols together; the module's actual 263+263 join surface is declared separately in the ObjTp=Symbol header as InputCueN=/OutputCueN= fields.

findings.implication: A converter targeting 'the 308 signals' would be mapping the wrong artifact - those are private wiring, not the public interface. The join map (InputCue/OutputCue) is the correct target.

findings.claim: Of 263 declared inputs, only 93 are real named joins; the rest are [~UNUSED~] reserved slots or [~BeginGroup~]/[~EndGroup~] group-header markers. Of 263 declared outputs, only 193 are real named joins.

findings.claim: The companion PDF (Automate VX v1.0.pdf) is a complete, human-authored join reference with descriptions for every named join, and its join names/order match the .cmc's Cue strings exactly. It answered nearly all of this task's mapping work directly.

findings.claim: Confirmed (recount, at the Extron 'Commands' capability-group granularity): of Extron's 18 named capabilities (AutoSwitch, ConnectionStatus, CameraPresetRecall, CameraPresetSave, ForceRoomConfiguration, HomeShotPreset, ISORecording, Layout, Output, PanTilt, Record, RoomConfiguration, Scenario, Sleep, Stream, SwitchCamera, Wake, Zoom), exactly 17 have at least one corresponding Crestron join; CameraPresetSave is the sole capability with zero join anywhere in the 93+193.

findings.claim: Several joins with no page anywhere on the documentation site correspond to real, live endpoints confirmed by the Extron ControlScript module's literal wire strings: Toggle/Start/Stop_AutoSwitch -> api/StartAutoSwitch, api/StopAutoSwitch; Start/Stop_ISO_Recording -> api/StartISORecord, api/StopISORecord; Wake -> api/Wake; Change_Room_Config -> api/ChangeRoomConfiguration (distinct from the documented Force variant).

findings.implication: This is independent, ground-truth (device-interoperating) confirmation that the public documentation is incomplete beyond what the harvest agent already flagged via GetAllStatus - it's not just that these joins might do something extra, they demonstrably call real endpoints the doc omits entirely.

findings.claim: The 8 undocumented sub-APIs the harvest already found inside GetAllStatus's example response (AutoSwitchStatus, OutputStatus, ISORecordStatus, RecordStatus, CopyStatus, GetLayouts, LayoutStatus, GetRoomConfigs, RoomConfigStatus) all have a plausible or exact-name-match join in the .cmc (Get_AutoSwitch_Status, Get_Output_Status, Get_ISO_Record_Status, Get_Record_Status, Get_Copy_Files_Status, Get_Layouts, Get_Current_Layout, Get_Room_Configs, Get_Current_Room_Config), and several of these are confirmed real by exact-string match in the Extron ControlScript module too (api/AutoSwitchStatus, api/OutputStatus, api/ISORecordStatus, api/RecordStatus, api/RoomConfigStatus).
findings.evidence: /tmp/input_cues.tsv rows 15,37,27,21,231,72,70,106,104; samples/Automate VX/Controlscript/onebynd_sm_Automate_VX_Series_v1_0_11_0.py lines 93,205,162,266,289
findings.implication: The Crestron macro's author (or 1Beyond, who likely supplied the driver spec to both vendors) had access to a fuller internal API surface than what the public Crestron SDK doc site now shows - three independent artifacts (doc's own GetAllStatus example, Extron wire strings, Crestron join names) triangulate on the same undocumented endpoints.

findings.claim: The two 'no way to poll' facts the PDF states explicitly line up with true API gaps: Selected_Camera_Preset_FB is documented in the PDF as having 'no way to poll for this information' (client-tracked only), and CameraStatus's ShotStatus fields are scattered across several joins rather than exposed as one, matching that ShotStatus itself has no dedicated join.

findings.implication: Even the module's own documentation acknowledges specific reachability gaps consistent with the API's documented limitations, which is a useful sanity check that this isn't the .cmc's own omission but a real device/API constraint.

findings.claim: Coverage tally against the documented 32 endpoints: ~21 have a clean, high-confidence 1:1 (or 1:N enum-expanded) join; ~6 more are reachable only through inference or partial exposure (GetAllStatus, GetCameras [Camera_Count only, no id/name/ip], ScenarioStatus, ShotStatus, StopPT, StopZ); 5 have zero join anywhere (GetActiveTalkers, ImportCameraPresets, Macro, Restart, SaveCameraPreset).
findings.evidence: /tmp/spec-vs-cmc-join-map.tsv (full row-by-row mapping); reference/automate-vx-api/ENDPOINTS.md 32-row table cross-referenced against /tmp/input_cues.tsv and /tmp/output_cues.tsv
findings.implication: Roughly two-thirds of the documented API is cleanly reachable through the SIMPL join surface; the rest is either aggregated behind other joins, dependent on unverifiable release-edge behavior (PT/Z stop), or simply not exposed to the touchpanel programmer at all.

findings.claim: The join-naming translation from API CamelCase to SIMPL Title_Case_With_Underscores is recognizable but not mechanically invertible: it requires human judgment for (a) enum-expansion decisions (ChangeLayout's 26-letter id became 25 separate pulse joins; the 99-value RoomConfig id stayed a single analog join - a size-dependent choice), (b) contextual splitting of one endpoint into two joins (CallCameraPreset -> Call_Live_Camera_Preset / Call_Selected_Camera_Preset, driven by a SIMPL-side 'selected camera' concept absent from the API spec), (c) deliberate omission of endpoints (SaveCameraPreset, Restart, Macro, ImportCameraPresets, GetActiveTalkers never got a join at all), and (d) convenience joins with no API equivalent (Toggle_* joins implying client-side state tracking that must call Start or Stop).
findings.evidence: /tmp/input_cues.tsv rows 44-68 (Change_Layout_A..Y) vs row 100/102 (single Change_Room_Config / Force_Room_Config); rows 223 and 225 (Call_Live_Camera_Preset, Call_Selected_Camera_Preset) both mapping to the single documented CallCameraPreset endpoint per reference/automate-vx-api/ENDPOINTS.md
findings.implication: A generator could auto-produce a baseline join map (verb+CamelCase-to-Title_Case, one join per documented param) for the ~21 simple 1:1 endpoints, but the enum-expansion threshold, the contextual splits, and the omission/inclusion decisions are UX judgment calls a human made, not derivable purely from the API's request/response shapes.

Whether the Crestron macro's apparent superset knowledge of undocumented endpoints (AutoSwitch*, ISORecord*, Wake, ChangeRoomConfiguration) came from a 1Beyond-supplied spec shared with both Crestron and Extron, or from earlier/different documentation than what's on the current SDK site - the .cmc's SmplCName/DbVr metadata gives no vendor-relationship provenance.

# Synthesis — Automate VX as spec-vs-implementation, and what it says about the project's centre of gravity

## 1. Could a working driver be generated from the vendor API doc alone?

Partly, and the shortfall is exactly the part that matters.

Start with the coverage arithmetic, because a claim in `findings/07` has been quietly propping up a wrong intuition. The harvest reports 32 documented endpoints and `findings/07-1beyond-and-simpl.md:80` reports "32 identical endpoint strings" shared by the two Extron implementations, and the harvest treats the match as corroboration that its enumeration is complete. **The two 32s are different sets.** The doc table's 32 rows include `Get-Token`, so it documents 31 `/api/` paths (`reference/automate-vx-api/ENDPOINTS.md`, endpoint table); Extron's ControlScript module contains 32 `/api/` paths plus `get-token` — 33 strings. A set diff of the two gives 22 in common, 10 documented-but-never-called, 11 called-but-not-in-the-table. The numerical coincidence is meaningless; the overlap is 22/33 of what Extron ships and 22/32 of what Crestron publishes.

What a doc-driven generator would get right is the whole mechanical surface: POST-only, JSON in and out, base `https://host:4443`, `/api/` prefix with `get-token` at the root, and the auth handshake — base64(`user:pass`) to obtain a token, then the raw token echoed in `Authorization` on every call, **with no scheme prefix**. Extron does exactly this (`samples/Automate VX/Controlscript/onebynd_sm_Automate_VX_Series_v1_0_11_0.py:57,432,437,476`), and the spec's own cURL shows `-H "Authorization: YWRtaW46MWJleW9uZA=="` (`reference/automate-vx-api/API-Reference/Get-Token-API.md`). Note that our own `ENDPOINTS.md` labels 31 rows "Bearer token"; a generator that trusted that summary rather than the source page would emit `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and fail to interoperate. That is a one-line demonstration of how doc-derived intermediate artifacts introduce their own defects.

What it would miss:

**Endpoints that only device contact reveals.** Five strings in the shipping Extron driver have zero trace anywhere in the 40 harvested pages: `StartAutoSwitch` and `StopAutoSwitch` (:78-79), `StartISORecord`/`StopISORecord` (:147-148), and `Wake` (:382) — the mirror of documented `Sleep`. Six more exist only inside example bodies: the five `*Status` sub-APIs Extron polls (`AutoSwitchStatus`:93, `OutputStatus`:205, `ISORecordStatus`:162, `RecordStatus`:266, `RoomConfigStatus`:289), which appear only in `GetAllStatus`'s sample JSON, and `ChangeRoomConfiguration`, which appears only as a batched call name in `reference/automate-vx-api/API-Reference/Macro-API.md:57`. The earlier claim that six endpoints had no doc trace at all is one too many; `ChangeRoomConfiguration` belongs with the example-only group.

**Types that are per-field, not per-policy.** The spec types `GoToScenario.id` as int; Extron sends `{'id': str(value)}` (:302, identical in the .pkp script). But two lines of context away, `ManualSwitchCamera.address` is passed through unconverted (:360) — so this is not a blanket "stringify everything" house style, it is a field-by-field accommodation of live firmware. No amount of doc reading produces that.

**Error handling that the spec itself makes contradictory.** Extron's response check is `if res['status'] == 'Error'` (:413). `StopPT` and `StopZ` are the only endpoints that return lowercase `"status": "error"` with `message` instead of `err` (`reference/automate-vx-api/API-Reference/StopPT-API.md:73`). So Extron's shipping driver silently treats a failed pan/tilt or zoom stop as success. That bug is invisible from either vendor artifact and falls straight out of having the spec — which is itself the strongest argument for spec-anchored work.

**Everything that isn't an endpoint.** The ControlScript module is 639 lines; 33 of them are wire strings. Roughly 200 lines (`:420-623`) are transport, token re-auth, subscription, status cache and feedback plumbing, and another large block is `ValueStateValues` mapping between wire JSON (`results: false`) and control-system state strings (`'Off'`) — for example `:84-100` and `:196-212`. None of that is in the API doc; all of it is target-framework shape.

The historical evidence is decisive and slightly humbling: the `.pkp`-embedded script's header cites page numbers of earlier revisions of *this same document* (`# Pg 6`, `# Pg 12 & 14`, "Automate API - 2023-12-28.pdf"), and Extron's engineers, working from that PDF, still logged ten dated revision entries between 07/15/2019 and 07/20/2026 with DR ticket numbers attached to additions like Sleep/Wake and Force Room Configuration. Doc-driven generation was tried by the vendor, with the document in hand, and it converged only through field iteration.

**Implication for centre of gravity.** The question is a false binary. Spec-driven generation produces a good scaffold and — more valuably — a *coverage oracle*. Format conversion produces the field-tested deltas that no spec contains. The project's leverage is in the join: a converter that emits a coverage diff (documented / implemented / both / neither, plus type and shape mismatches) as a first-class output is worth more than either generator alone, because it turns "did we get everything?" from a judgement call into a set operation.

## 2. What the spec adds that neither vendor artifact carried

Ten endpoints nobody implemented: `CopyFiles`, `GetActiveTalkers`, `GetAllStatus`, `GetCameras`, `GetScenarios`, `ImportCameraPresets`, `Macro`, `RecordingSpaceAvail`, `Restart`, `ShotStatus`. Most are installer-time or batch conveniences, but `GetActiveTalkers` and `ShotStatus` are live control-relevant state that neither Extron nor the Crestron join surface exposes.

Parameter semantics, not just ranges: `ptDir` 0–7 mapped to compass directions, `zDir` 0/1, and the behavioural difference between documented `ForceChangeRoomConfig` ("AutoSwitching is paused then resumed") and the undocumented non-forcing `ChangeRoomConfiguration` that Extron actually calls. Extron's code encodes the ranges; only the spec explains why there are two.

Operational facts with no representation in any driver: tokens do not expire but are bound to the client's source IP, so a re-IP requires re-auth (`reference/automate-vx-api/Quick-Start/Authentication.md`). And a currency signal — `CallPlugin` was removed (`reference/automate-vx-api/Whats-New/Whats-New.md:19`) while the Crestron macro still exposes `Call_Plugin_1/2/3` joins. The spec dates the artifact.

It also adds a caution about machine-consuming vendor docs. The `Macro` example body is malformed JSON containing a leaked developer's name (`"body": "{\"id\": behnam}"`, `Macro-API.md:57`). `CameraStatus-API.md:51` documents `"address": "[value]"` while `GetAllStatus-API.md:51` shows the same call returning `"address":1,"addresses":[1]`; `GetCameras-API.md:51` documents `{id,name,ip}` while the aggregate example shows `{id,model}`. Extron codes defensively around this (`res['address']` then `int(value)`, :372-374). A strict-typed generator would not.

## 3. Is a SIMPL join surface mechanically derivable from an API spec?

The structure first, because `findings/07` describes it wrongly. The 308 `ObjTp=Sg` blocks are not private internal wiring: 286 of the 308 names are byte-identical to the 286 real named joins (93 named inputs of 263 slots, 193 named outputs of 263), with zero joins missing from the `Sg` set. The 22 remainder are 10 group-divider markers, one `[~UNUSED~]`, ten `Camera_*_Debounced` helpers and one `//Automate_Debug`. And the macro places **8** `ObjTp=Sm` sub-symbols, not three (`grep -c '^ObjTp=Sm'` on `samples/Automate VX/Crestron Module/1Beyond Automate_VX_v1.2.cmc`). The "I/O contract plus a dangling pointer" verdict survives — the protocol logic is still in the unshipped `.csp` — but the internals are better characterised than the finding says. `Room_Config_90_Name$`, cited there as an internal wire, is `OutputCue195` (`:1074`) and its `Sg` block at `:3766`; it is a public join.

Derivable mechanically: the name transform (CamelCase → `Title_Case_With_Underscores`), signal type from parameter type, and a status join per status endpoint. Call it a 60–70% first draft.

Not derivable, because they are UX judgements:

Enum expansion threshold. `ChangeLayout`'s A–Z `id` became 25 discrete pulse joins (`InputCue44=Change_Layout_A` onward); `ForceChangeRoomConfig`'s 1–99 `id` stayed a single analog join (`InputCue100`, `:716`). Identical spec shape, opposite encodings, decided by cardinality.

Contextual splitting. The single `CallCameraPreset` endpoint became two joins — `Call_Live_Camera_Preset` (`InputCue223`) and `Call_Selected_Camera_Preset` (`InputCue225`) — because SIMPL introduces a "selected camera" concept the API has no notion of.

Convenience joins that imply client state. `Toggle_AutoSwitch`, `Toggle_Recording`, `Toggle_ISO_Recording`, `Toggle_Stream`, `Toggle_Output` (`InputCue12/17/24/29/34`) each require poll-then-branch logic; the API has only Start and Stop. Similarly the ten debounce signals wrapping the joystick inputs exist for panel ergonomics, not protocol.

Omissions and padding. `SaveCameraPreset`, `Restart`, `Macro`, `ImportCameraPresets` and `GetActiveTalkers` got no join at all, and 160 of 263 input slots are `[~UNUSED~]` reserve. Finally, `Selected_Camera_Preset_FB` is documented in the companion PDF as having "currently no way to poll for this information" — a client-tracked feedback that exists precisely because the API lacks it.

So: derive a baseline, then apply a policy file (expansion threshold, toggle policy, name-array padding, omission list). And note the practical shortcut this device demonstrates — the vendor already published the full join table as a PDF whose entries match the `.cmc` cue strings verbatim. Parsing the vendor's own join document beats inferring one.

## 4. P20 vs I20 — bounded residue, and the earlier framing needs splitting

I re-ran the referenced-minus-declared check on both cameras and on Samsung. Both cameras reference 39 distinct transformation names. P20 declares 27, leaving 12 undeclared; I20 declares 26, leaving 13. The undeclared sets are identical except for one name.

The important correction: **the undeclared set is not all "IL residue".** It splits cleanly in two. Seven names — `Divide`, `Sum`, `Subtract`, `Product`, `Identity`, `ViscaAssemble4LowerNibbles`, `ViscaExtractNibbles` — are referenced by *both* drivers and implemented by *neither*; they have no TypeDef, MethodDef or even TypeRef in either DLL, so they resolve at runtime from `Crestron.DeviceDrivers.SDK` 26.0.26.0. Those are catalogue-wide framework built-ins: implement once, reuse forever, and four of them are arithmetic. The genuinely driver-local IL is five types on P20 and six on I20, confirmed by `strings` on both assemblies: `FormatRomVersion`, `ParseDecimal`, `ZoomLevelToPosition`, `ZoomPositionToLevel`, `ApplyZoomPositionStep` and an `OverridePolynomial` pair on both, with I20 alone adding `ViscaAssemble2LowerNibbles`.

Two further corrections to the earlier account. `OverridePolynomial` is not an uninvoked hook — it registers two types (transformation and transform-info) under the literal string `Polynomial`, i.e. it supplies the runtime implementation for the JSON's declaratively-typed `Polynomial` transformations, which is why the `ImplementationProviderAttribute` row count is 7 on P20 and 8 on I20 rather than 6 and 7. And the six-name list in `findings/07:31-33` is the I20 set specifically; it should not be read as a generic figure.

The strongest evidence for bounded-ness is the delta itself: two camera generations from the same vendor differ by exactly one transformation, and it is a nibble-width variant of the same VISCA packer. Meanwhile Samsung's schema-1.0.0.0 IP and Serial packages reference 16 and 15 transformations and declare every one — zero residue. So the residue is a V2 Entity Model phenomenon, and within a product family it is a fixed small family with one swappable protocol-codec slot.

Honest limit: n = 2 cameras, one vendor, one line, plus one display. That is enough to refute "unbounded per-device code" and not enough to size the catalogue. The test is cheap and mechanical — run referenced-minus-declared over every V2 package obtainable and see whether the undeclared names converge on a closed vocabulary. If they do, the converter implements the SDK vocabulary once and flags only the genuinely local names, which is a tractable amount of decompilation per driver rather than per method.

## 5. What should change in findings 02–07, and the single next step

`findings/07` needs the most work. The "32 identical endpoint strings" fact stays (it was reproduced independently against the `.pkp`'s NRBF object 415), but the sentence at `:80` must stop implying it matches the documented 32 — the correct statement is 21 shared `/api/` paths plus `get-token`, 11 Extron-only, 10 documented-unimplemented. The `.cmc` paragraph at `:60-61` needs the structural fix: 286 of the 308 `Sg` names *are* the joins, and there are 8 placed sub-symbols, not three. The "semantic parity except `CameraPresetSave`" claim (`:93-96`) should be labelled as true at Extron's 18-capability grain only; at endpoint grain five endpoints have no join. The transformation section should adopt the built-in / driver-local split above and cite P20 as the second data point.

`findings/06`'s generalisation question gains real evidence: the referenced-minus-declared rule now has three data points, and the "fail loudly with the list of IL-only names" design rule from 07 should be amended to subtract the SDK built-in vocabulary first — otherwise the extractor cries wolf on `Sum` and `Divide` and buries the names that actually need decompiling.

`findings/04`'s "SIMPL is program logic, not a driver" ruling stands and needs only two additions: the `.cmc` is a *derivable-ish* I/O contract (which slightly raises the value of reading one, without changing the emission target away from `.pkg`), and this sample is stale against current firmware, evidenced by its `Call_Plugin` joins against `Whats-New.md:19`.

`findings/02` and `03` are unaffected; the Automate VX work incidentally re-confirms 02's Python-to-Python premise, since A and B are string-identical. `findings/05`'s Samsung cross-vendor claim is neither strengthened nor weakened here — this case could not test two vendors independently encoding a wire protocol — but it is worth recording that Samsung is the corpus's cleanest conversion case precisely because its schema 1.0 driver declares every transformation it uses.

Two defects in our own `reference/automate-vx-api/ENDPOINTS.md` should be fixed before anything consumes it: it says "8 sub-APIs" and lists nine, and it labels auth "Bearer token" on 31 rows when the spec uses no scheme prefix.

**Highest-value next step: build the three-way coverage differ.** A small tool that takes a spec endpoint set (including names mined out of example bodies, which is where six of Extron's eleven extras live), plus any number of implementation artifacts via the existing `pkp_dump.py` / `pkg_dump.py` extractors, and emits four buckets — implemented-and-documented, implemented-undocumented, documented-unimplemented, and parameter/response shape mismatches. It needs no new samples, it is a day's work (I recomputed the Automate VX endpoint diff in a single shell pipeline), it converts the project's dump tools into a measurement instrument, and its first run on this device already produces a shippable result: the `StopPT`/`StopZ` lowercase-`error` bug in Extron's shipping driver. That bucket output is simultaneously the generator's checklist and the converter's fidelity report, which is the artifact both halves of the strategy need.
